stories.title: Set up the TypeScript + Vite project with lint, type check and unit tests
stories.description: Create the project skeleton: package.json (exact dependency versions), package-lock.json, tsconfig.json (strict), vite.config.ts (dev server on port 5173 with strictPort), eslint.config.js (flat config with typescript-eslint), vitest.config.ts (unit tests are tests/**/*.test.ts; tests/e2e/ is excluded), index.html with the title 'Spine Fluoro Trainer', a minimal src/app/main.ts, and one first unit test in tests/core/. Dependencies: typescript, vite, three, @types/three, vitest, eslint, typescript-eslint, and @playwright/test pinned to exactly 1.63.0 (used from F0-S2; do NOT run 'playwright install'). npm scripts: dev, build, test (vitest run), lint (eslint + tsc --noEmit), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), and check (for now: lint, typecheck and test; F0-S2 adds screen tests). SHARED FILES: this story creates package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, eslint.config.js, vitest.config.ts and index.html, and is explicitly allowed to. No test suite exists before this story; a failing baseline in step 3 is expected and is not a separate fix.
acceptance: npm install completes without errors and creates package-lock.json
package.json pins @playwright/test to exactly 1.63.0 and every other dependency to an exact version (no ^ or ~)
npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test and npm run build all pass
index.html has <title>Spine Fluoro Trainer</title>
vite.config.ts serves the dev server on port 5173 and fails rather than switching port if 5173 is taken (strictPort)
npm test runs at least one unit test from tests/ and ignores tests/e2e/
stories.verify: npm install && npm run check && npm run build

stories.title: Set up Playwright screen tests in a desktop and a tablet set-up
stories.description: Add playwright.config.ts with two projects that every screen test runs in: 'desktop' (Chromium, 1280×800, mouse + keyboard) and 'tablet' (Chromium, 1024×768, hasTouch: true, isMobile: true). Screen tests are tests/e2e/**/*.spec.ts. The config starts the app with 'npm run dev' on http://localhost:5173 (webServer, reuse an existing server locally), sets trace to 'off', and passes the Chromium launch flags needed for WebGL2 on the software GPU (e.g. --use-angle=swiftshader, --enable-unsafe-swiftshader — see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Known technical risks). Add the npm script test:e2e (playwright test) and extend check to run lint, typecheck, unit tests and screen tests in that order. Add the first screen tests in tests/e2e/app/: the page title is 'Spine Fluoro Trainer', and a WebGL2 context can be created in the page. Never run 'playwright install': Chromium for 1.63.0 is pre-installed. SHARED FILES: creates playwright.config.ts and changes the scripts in package.json; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: npm run test:e2e runs every screen test twice: once in the 'desktop' project and once in the 'tablet' project
A screen test opens http://localhost:5173 and checks the page title is exactly 'Spine Fluoro Trainer' (passes in both projects)
A screen test checks that document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl2') is not null (passes in both projects)
npm run check runs lint, type check, unit tests and screen tests, and passes
stories.verify: npx playwright test tests/e2e/app && npm run check

stories.title: Add the anatomy:convert command with a placeholder converter
stories.description: Add the npm script anatomy:convert ("tsx tools/anatomy/convert.ts") and the dev dependency tsx (exact version), which runs TypeScript files directly in Node. Create tools/anatomy/convert.ts as a placeholder: it takes <input-folder> <output-folder>; when either is missing it prints a usage line containing '<input-folder> <output-folder>' and exits with a non-zero code; otherwise it prints that conversion is not built yet (F1) and exits with a non-zero code. F1 replaces the body; the test below must stay true after F1, so it only checks the missing-arguments case. The test starts the script with Node's child_process using a fixed argument list (no shell, no string gluing). Make sure lint and type check cover tools/. SHARED FILES: changes package.json and package-lock.json (dependency + script) and may change tsconfig.json/eslint.config.js to include tools/; explicitly allowed. Done in F0 so F1 never has to touch package.json while other loops run (owner decision 2026-11-09).
acceptance: package.json has the script anatomy:convert and tsx as an exact-version dev dependency
Unit test: running the command with no arguments prints a usage line containing '<input-folder> <output-folder>' and exits with a non-zero code
tools/anatomy/convert.ts passes lint and type check
Unit tests in tests/anatomy/convert-cli.test.ts pass
stories.verify: npm install && npx vitest run tests/anatomy/convert-cli.test.ts && npm run lint

stories.title: Add the shared tissue labels, vertebral levels and shared types
stories.description: Create src/core/labels.ts and src/core/types.ts, the contracts every later feature builds on. labels.ts: a numbered list of tissue labels (8-bit ids, 0 = air) with a short id and a display name, containing at least: air, skin/fat (one label), muscle, cortical bone, cancellous bone, disc, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, thecal sac, spinal cord, nerve root, artery, vein and joint space; plus helpers such as isBone(label). It also lists the vertebral level codes used by the level volume (C1…C7, T1…T12, L1…L5, sacrum, ilium; 0 = no level) and sides (left/right; +x is the patient's left). types.ts: the shared types named in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, with only the fields the spec needs: Volume (size, voxel spacing in mm, origin/orientation, region name, 8-bit intensity, 8-bit labels, optional 8-bit levels — F1.1, F1.3, F1.6); CArmPose (oblique and tilt in degrees, table left/right, head/foot and height in mm — F3.1); NeedleState (needle id, pre-bend, entry point, hub angles, bevel angle, inserted depth, shaft curve points, tip — F4, F5); TissueEvent (type: lossOfResistance, boneContact, duralPuncture, nerveContact, intravascular, cordContact, injection; time; tip position; message; optional level/side/volume/compartment — F6.2, F6.3, F9.6); AttemptRecord (procedure, mode, date, score parts, unsafe flag, shots, fluoro time — F10.5). Follow the coordinate and unit conventions in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Conventions (document them in comments). SHARED FILES: creates files in src/core/; explicitly allowed. Later features can only change these through an interactive session, so check every field against the spec.
acceptance: labels.ts exports every tissue label listed in F0.4, each with a unique id from 0 to 255; air is 0
labels.ts exports the level codes C1–C7, T1–T12, L1–L5, sacrum and ilium with unique ids from 1 to 255, and 0 means no level
isBone() is true for cortical and cancellous bone only
types.ts exports Volume, CArmPose, NeedleState, TissueEvent and AttemptRecord; a unit test builds one valid example of each and passes the type check
Unit tests in tests/core/labels.test.ts pass
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/core/labels.test.ts && npm run typecheck

stories.title: Add the central state store, event bus and seeded random numbers
stories.description: Create src/core/store.ts (one central store holding the shared state: current C-arm pose — default 0°/0° with the table at 0 —, shot count, last image pose (none until the first image), and the current volume; get, set and subscribe) with a small typed event bus (emit/on/off; events include 'exposure'), and src/core/random.ts (a seeded random number generator: the same seed gives the same sequence). Plain TypeScript, no screen code. SHARED FILES: creates files in src/core/; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: The store starts with pose oblique 0°, tilt 0°, table offsets 0 mm, shot count 0 and no last image pose
set() updates the state and calls subscribers once per change; unsubscribing stops the calls
An 'exposure' event emitted on the bus reaches every listener registered with on(), and none after off()
random.ts: two generators with the same seed give identical sequences of 1000 numbers; different seeds give different sequences; every value is in [0, 1)
Unit tests in tests/core/store.test.ts and tests/core/random.test.ts pass

stories.title: Generate the synthetic phantom volume
stories.description: Create src/core/phantom.ts: a function that generates a small, deterministic, labelled Volume (no larger than 128×128×128 voxels) used by all tests instead of the real CT. It contains every tissue label in src/core/labels.ts, and two vertebra-like blocks (cortical shell, cancellous inside, a disc between the bodies) with a foramen between them containing nerve root voxels on both sides, a joint space between the two blocks' posterior parts, a thecal sac with spinal cord inside, epidural space and ligamentum flavum behind it, muscle, a skin/fat layer and air around it, plus an artery and a vein. It also fills the 8-bit intensity volume (bone densest, air lowest, soft tissue in between) and the levels volume (each block's bone voxels get a lumbar level, e.g. L4 and L5; no other voxel has a level). Export documented test points: the vertebra block centres, the foramen centres, and a midline back-to-front test line between the two blocks' posterior parts (interlaminar). Follow docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Conventions (+y = posterior, mm). SHARED FILES: creates a file in src/core/; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: The phantom is no larger than 128×128×128 voxels and has positive voxel spacing in mm
Every tissue label exported by labels.ts occurs at least once in the phantom
Walking the exported midline test line from the back (+y) to the front, the first occurrences of skin/fat, muscle, ligamentum flavum, epidural space and thecal sac come in exactly that order
The label at each exported vertebra block centre is bone (cortical or cancellous), and the level there is that block's level
Each foramen has nerve root voxels on both the left and right side
Every bone voxel has a level and no non-bone voxel does
The mean intensity of bone voxels is higher than that of muscle, which is higher than that of air
Two calls give identical volumes (deterministic)
Unit tests in tests/core/phantom.test.ts pass

stories.title: Add C-arm projection geometry (pose to source, detector, project and unproject)
stories.description: Create src/core/geometry.ts: given a CArmPose, compute the X-ray source position, the detector plane and a 512×512 pixel grid, and provide project(point) → pixel and unproject(pixel) → ray (origin + direction). Patient prone; the isocentre is the origin of the table-relative frame; table offsets move the patient relative to the isocentre; oblique rotates about the patient's long axis (z), tilt (cranial/caudal) about the left-right axis (x). Use typical mobile C-arm distances (owner decision 2026-11-09: typical values, no specific machine) (source-to-detector and source-to-isocentre distance, detector size) as exported, commented named constants; the tests do not depend on their exact values. Degrees in the public API, radians only inside. Document the sign conventions (which side the source is on at +90° oblique, which way is image up) in comments. SHARED FILES: creates a file in src/core/; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: For at least 20 poses spread across oblique −90…+90° and tilt −40…+40° (table at 0), the isocentre projects to the image centre (within 0.5 px)
For random points inside the phantom and at least 10 poses, projecting a point and then unprojecting the pixel gives a ray that passes within 0.1 mm of the original point

At pose (0°, 0°) the beam is a straight AP beam for a prone patient: the source is anterior (−y, under the table), the detector is posterior (+y, above the back), and the central ray is parallel to the y axis
At oblique +90° (tilt 0°) the central ray is parallel to the x axis (lateral beam)
Unit tests in tests/core/geometry.test.ts pass

stories.title: Add the window.__sim test hook, present in development and absent from the production build
stories.description: Create src/core/testHook.ts: when import.meta.env.DEV is true (npm run dev, which the screen tests use), it creates window.__sim with getState() returning the C-arm pose, the shot count and the last image's pose (read from the store), and a way for zones to register more read-only getters. stories.title: Add a WebGL2 canvas to the fluoro panel that redraws on each exposure, with a pixel read-back test helper
stories.description: In the render zone, put a 512×512 WebGL2 canvas (via Three.js, test id fluoro-canvas) in the fluoro panel. It shows a blank screen until the first image, and draws a frame on every 'exposure' event (for now a flat fill is enough; the DRR comes in F0-S12). Make the pixels readable by screen tests (e.g. preserveDrawingBuffer, or reading right after drawing). Add a shared screen-test helper tests/fixtures/readCanvas.ts that returns the canvas pixels as grey values 0–255 at given (x, y) positions in the 512×512 image. This story de-risks reading WebGL pixels on the software GPU before the real shader is written. SHARED FILES: creates tests/fixtures/readCanvas.ts; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): after accepting the disclaimer, the fluoro panel contains a canvas with a 512×512 drawing size
Screen test (both set-ups): readCanvas returns values in 0–255 for the corners and centre of the image
Screen test (both set-ups): the pixels after taking an image differ from the blank screen shown before the first image
Screen tests in tests/e2e/render/canvas.spec.ts pass in both set-ups

stories.title: Render a GPU DRR of the phantom on each exposure, with bone dark and air light
stories.description: In the render zone, replace the flat fill with a minimal GPU DRR: upload the store's volume intensity as a 3D texture (Three.js Data3DTexture), and in a fragment shader march each pixel's ray from the X-ray source to the detector using src/core/geometry.ts (same pose, same 512×512 grid), add up absorption from the intensity values, and display brightness = e^(−total absorption) so that more absorption is darker (bone dark, air light). Only the fluoro panel's rendering changes; noise, collimation, magnification, flips and the CPU reference are F2, not this story. The screen test computes the expected pixel by importing src/core/geometry.ts and src/core/phantom.ts in the test itself (they are plain TypeScript), projecting a vertebra block centre at the image's pose.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop, spacebar) and (tablet, tap 'Shot'): after one image at the default pose, the grey value at the projected centre of a phantom vertebra block is at least 50 lower (darker) than the grey value at an image corner (air)
npm run check passes (lint, type check, unit tests and screen tests in both set-ups)
stories.verify: npx playwright test tests/e2e/render/drr.spec.ts && npm run check
